items.title: People in China are spending nearly as much of their income as Americans on healthcare
items.summary: BEIJING — High healthcare costs are a big factor driving people in China to save, rather than spend, their money, the International Monetary Fund pointed out in a new book titled "Toward a New Economic Growth Model for China."

items.title: Harvard’s endowment jumps 27% in fiscal 2026, lifted by SpaceX as top holding
items.summary: Harvard University's endowment grew 27.1% in fiscal year 2026, its strongest return in five years, the school said in its annual financial report released on Thursday.

items.title: China indicates rare earths will keep flowing to EU, regardless of U.S. trade deal expiration
items.summary: BEIJING — China intends to keep exporting rare earths to Europe regardless of whether a U.S. trade deal with Beijing gets extended past January.

items.title: Economists: Hot PPI shows Fed's work is not done
items.summary: Wall Street estimates for the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation indicator now expect an acceleration from the level that prompted the central bank to hike rates last month.

items.title: U.S. Treasury dismisses IMF debt warning and 'messy' forecasting
items.summary: The International Monetary Fund should check its own forecasting record before criticizing U.S. fiscal policy, David Zervos, newly appointed counselor to the Treasury Secretary , said on Thursday.

items.title: Wholesale prices jumped 6.3% annually in September, biggest gain since 2022
items.summary: September's producer price index came in much hotter than economists forecast on Thursday, underscoring the continued inflationary pressure from energy amid the U.S. war with Iran.

items.title: Analysis: Why a $2 trillion deficit and 5% Treasury yields are becoming America's biggest economic challenge
items.summary: Long-term bond yields above 5% and a $2 trillion deficit are giving Americans a taste of what a U.S. debt crisis would be like.

items.title: UK economy grew 0.1% in August, beating expectations
items.summary: The U.K. economy grew by a better-than-expected 0.1% in the month to August, with production growth offsetting weak output in services and construction.

items.title: In charts: How one of the world's biggest economies got trapped by debt
items.summary: France's parliament begins debate on the 2027 budget Tuesday as high deficits, rising debt and student protests sharpen the political cost of fiscal consolidation.
